Strategic focus: Neuter nominative agreement. 'Возможное' takes the neuter ending to match 'решение'. The problem-solving phrase roots the neuter form.
Strategic focus: Plural accusative agreement. 'Возможные' matches inanimate plural 'пути', so the accusative looks like the nominative. The deliberation scene fixes the plural form.
Strategic focus: Masculine dative agreement. After 'к', 'возможному' takes the masculine dative ending to match 'дождю'. The weather prep grounds the oblique form.
Strategic focus: Feminine prepositional agreement. After 'о', 'возможной' takes the feminine prepositional ending to match 'опасности'. The medical warning anchors the oblique case.
Strategic focus: Masculine genitive agreement. After negated 'нет', 'возможного' takes the masculine genitive ending to match 'выхода'. The tense scene shows the genitive in use.
Strategic focus: Plural accusative agreement. 'Возможные' matches inanimate plural 'последствия', so the accusative mirrors the nominative. The research scene roots the plural form.
Strategic focus: Short-form neuter as adverbial predicate. 'Возможно' is the neuter short form used impersonally to mean 'it is possible'. This is the most common everyday use of the adjective.
Strategic focus: Short-form neuter as a sentence adverb. 'Возможно' here works as 'maybe', a frozen neuter form opening the sentence. It shows the form drifting toward an adverb in speech.
